ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: All UBOs, directors, and senior managers must undergo comprehensive screening against the New Zealand Police Financial Intelligence Unit's PEP list, the United Nations Security Council Consolidated List, the OFAC SDN List, and the New Zealand Sanctions List. Screening must be conducted at onboarding and on an ongoing basis using automated real-time tools and manual review. Enhanced due diligence is mandatory for any PEP, high-risk jurisdiction, or adverse media findings. Results must be documented, risk-rated, and retained for at least five years. Additionally, the company must implement a risk-based approach to customer due diligence, including verification of beneficial ownership and source of funds, and file suspicious transaction reports with the Financial Intelligence Unit as required.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: New Zealand Companies Office - Online Name Reservation Portal
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Names must be in English or Maori. If a Maori name is used, a phonetic transliteration in English may be required. The name must not be identical or nearly similar to an existing registered name. The four-tier naming convention assesses (1) exact match, (2) phonetic similarity, (3) visual similarity, and (4) semantic similarity. Transliteration from non-Latin scripts must be provided in English to facilitate review.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Companies Act 1993 (New Zealand), sections 12 to 18, 24, 25, 31, 32, 34, 35, 39 to 45, 51 to 57, 122, 123, 128, 130, 138, 149 to 154, 164 and 189, together with the Financial Reporting Act 2013.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: New Zealand Companies Office, Companies Register, Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment (MBIE)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Form 1 - Application for Registration of a Company (online incorporation application on the Companies Register)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: None prescribed under the Companies Act 1993. No blocked escrow account or minimum paid-up capital is required. The board fixes the share issue price and must satisfy the solvency and valuation requirements of sections 50 to 57 of the Companies Act 1993 whenever shares are issued for non-cash consideration.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: MINUTES OF THE FIRST MEETING OF THE BOARD OF DIRECTORS OF [COMPANY NAME] LIMITED, held at the registered office of the Company on the [date]. PRESENT: [director names]. IN ATTENDANCE: [secretary if any]. The Chair confirmed that a quorum was present and declared the meeting duly constituted. After due deliberation, the following resolutions were proposed, seconded and passed unanimously. 1. REGISTERED OFFICE: RESOLVED that the registered office of the Company be established at [physical New Zealand address], which address is a physical, open and accessible place, not a postal-only box, and is hereby adopted for the service of documents and all statutory communications under section 189 of the Companies Act 1993. 2. SHARE CAPITAL: RESOLVED that the allotment and issue of the subscription shares set out in the incorporation application, comprising [number] ordinary shares of no par value, issued to the subscribers at the agreed subscription price, be and is hereby ratified, confirmed and approved, and such shares are recorded as fully paid in the share register. 3. BANKING: RESOLVED that the directors be and are hereby authorized to open, operate and maintain corporate bank accounts at any New Zealand registered bank, to appoint authorized signatories, to establish dual-signature thresholds for amounts exceeding NZD [threshold], and to transact all ordinary banking business of the Company. 4. OFFICERS: RESOLVED that [director names] be appointed as directors, that [name] be appointed Chief Executive Officer, and that [name] be appointed as Company Secretary if the Board so elects, each to serve until removed under the Companies Act 1993 or the Company's constitution. 5. DELEGATION: RESOLVED that any director or officer be and is hereby authorized on behalf of the Company to sign, execute, lodge and deliver all documents, applications and instruments necessary to implement and register the foregoing resolutions, including filings with the New Zealand Companies Office, registers of statutory records, and applications to the Inland Revenue Department for an IRD number, GST registration, and any tax or subsidy matters. 6. GENERAL: RESOLVED that these resolutions shall take effect immediately and remain in full force until revoked, amended or replaced by a subsequent board or shareholder resolution. The meeting was then closed.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name Search, Director Eligibility and Registered Office Preparation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: New Zealand Companies Office, Companies Register (online)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a preliminary name search on the Companies Register to confirm that the proposed company name is not identical or confusingly similar to an existing name. Reserve the selected name if required. Verify that the registered office address is physically located in New Zealand and is accessible by the public for service of documents. Confirm that at least one director is either resident in New Zealand or an Australian resident who qualifies under the Companies Act 1993. Obtain written consent from each proposed director. Prepare the business description for the ISIC 6201 software activity, the subscriber names, addresses, share percentages and the intended allotment details. Compile this information in a clean electronic dossier ready for the online incorporation application.
required_dossiers: Proposed company name and alternate names
List of proposed directors with addresses and consent to act
Shareholders names, addresses and shareholding percentages
Registered office address in New Zealand with physical accessibility confirmation
Brief business activity description for ISIC 6201
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the proposed name fails the availability check, file under an alternative name or apply for a name review under section 28 of the Companies Act 1993. If a director consent is defective, obtain a corrected consent and resubmit the online application within 20 working days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Online Incorporation Filing and Certificate of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: New Zealand Companies Office, Companies Register
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Lodge the incorporation application electronically through the Companies Register using a RealMe login or an authorized intermediary. Submit Form 1 with exact information on the company name, registered office, directors, shareholders, share structure and financial reporting period. Attach the constitution if a tailored constitution has been adopted; otherwise the default constitution under the Companies Act 1993 applies. Include each director's signed consent to act and the subscribers' share subscription details. Complete the overseas shareholding percentage fields, if any. Pay the prescribed filing fee by electronic payment. The Registrar will review the application and, upon compliance with statutory requirements, issue the Certificate of Incorporation together with the New Zealand Business Number (NZBN) and company number.
required_dossiers: Completed Form 1
Certificate or record of name reservation (if any)
Company constitution (optional)
Signed consent to act for each director
Subscriber and shareholder details with share subscription amounts
Payment of official filing fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar queries missing or inconsistent information, submit an electronic correction or resubmit through the Companies Register portal within 20 working days. If registration is suspended, use the Companies Office contact center to obtain the specific query, remedy the defect and pay any additional processing charges.

step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the incorporated company for an IRD number using the Inland Revenue's myIR portal or the Business Registration form. Provide the company's NZBN, company number, registered address, principal business description, expected annual turnover, GST registration preference, financial reporting period, and director information. For the AI avatar video generation SaaS activity under ISIC 6201, register for GST if taxable supplies exceed NZD 60,000 in any 12-month period, or elect voluntary GST registration if input credit recovery is beneficial. If employees will be engaged, register for PAYE, KiwiSaver and fringe benefit tax as appropriate. The IRD will issue the company's tax reference number and confirm the applicable filing frequencies.
required_dossiers: Certificate of incorporation
New Zealand Business Number (NZBN)
Company registered office and principal business address
Directors names, addresses and IRD identification
Estimated turnover and business activity description
Bank account details for tax refunds
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the IRD rejects or suspends the registration due to a data mismatch, correct the details in myIR or submit a paper amendment within 20 working days. If a tax obligation or registration date is disputed, file a notice of proposed adjustment or contact the IRD for binding guidance.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate Bank Account Opening and Signatory Mandate
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registered banks and authorized financial institutions under the Reserve Bank of New Zealand Act
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Present the executed pro-forma first board resolution to a New Zealand registered bank and complete the corporate onboarding process. Supply the certificate of incorporation, constitution, NZBN, director identification documents in original or certified form, proof of the registered office, and a written description of the SaaS revenue model and payment rails, including Stripe or Paddle. Complete the AML/CFT customer due diligence questionnaires, listing all shareholders and ultimate beneficial owners. Execute the bank account mandate and signatory cards, setting dual-signatory authorization for high-value payments. The bank will issue the corporate account details after compliance review, enabling deposit of share capital and payment of corporate expenses.
required_dossiers: First board resolution authorizing bank accounts
Certificate of incorporation and constitution
NZBN and company number confirmation
Director passports or government identification and proof of address
Beneficial ownership and source of funds declarations
SaaS business description and expected transaction volumes
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank requests enhanced due diligence, provide the requested corporate structure charts, source of funds evidence, and director declarations to the AML/CFT compliance team promptly. If the application is rejected, apply to another registered bank and retain records of any account refusal for the companies office review if required.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Statutory Records, Annual Return and Ongoing Governance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: New Zealand Companies Office and the board of directors
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Maintain the company's statutory records in a secure location, either physically at the registered office or electronically accessible in New Zealand. Create the shareholder register, director register, share allotment register, minute book and accounting records. Record all share issues and file a share allotment notice with the Companies Office within 10 working days of any post-incorporation allotment. File the annual return within 20 working days of the return date. Because the company is engaged in pure software and AIGC video generation under ISIC 6201, no physical industrial or environmental operating permits are required; this step focuses on corporate law compliance, financial reporting under the Financial Reporting Act 2013, and ongoing Inland Revenue filings.
required_dossiers: Shareholder register and director register
Register of share allotments
Minute book containing board resolutions
Accounting records and financial statements (if applicable)
Companies Office annual return
IRD tax filings and GST returns
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If an annual return is filed late, file the overdue return immediately and request removal of any penalty through the Companies Office compliance channel. For tax penalties, apply to Inland Revenue for remission under the Tax Administration Act 1994 and maintain full supporting records for employees and revenue.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Inland Revenue Department (IRD), the national tax authority of New Zealand; online portal: myIR at https://www.ird.govt.nz/myir/
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a foreign non-resident entity: (1) Determine whether the entity is carrying on a taxable business in New Zealand; if so, register the overseas company with the New Zealand Companies Office under the Companies Act 1993 and obtain a New Zealand Business Number (NZBN) where registration is required, using the foreign incorporation documents. (2) Apply to Inland Revenue through myIR for an IRD number as a non-resident company; if myIR self-service is not available for the entity type, submit the equivalent paper application to IRD. The application must state entity type, foreign tax residence, directors and shareholders, registered office, principal activities, and the expected date of commencing New Zealand activity. (3) Attach supporting documents including certificate of incorporation or overseas registration extract, constitution or charter, directorship resolutions, and evidence of non-resident status. (4) When the IRD number is issued, use the same IRD number as the GST registration number; register for GST separately through myIR if taxable supplies in New Zealand are or are expected to exceed the NZD 60,000 threshold, or voluntarily where input credit recovery is needed. (5) For a New Zealand-incorporated limited company, the Companies Office forwards entity data to Inland Revenue, and the company must complete its IRD number and GST registration details through myIR before filing obligations commence.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: A New Zealand limited company is taxed at the entity level. Eligible close companies may elect Look-Through Company (LTC) status under the Income Tax Act 2007, subject to the maximum five-shareholder rule and eligibility criteria, causing income and losses to be attributed to shareholders. No US-style check-the-box election exists in New Zealand; hybrid mismatch treatment is governed by statutory anti-avoidance rules, not elective.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Goods and Services Tax (GST) — value-added tax administered by Inland Revenue (IRD)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: NZD 60,000 of taxable supplies in New Zealand in any 12-month period; non-resident suppliers of remote services and digital services to New Zealand consumers are also required to register if their total New Zealand supplies exceed NZD 60,000 in 12 months. Voluntary registration is permitted.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No real-time fiscal clearance system, no mandatory API invoice stamping, and no anti-fraud digital stamping mandate exists in New Zealand. E-invoicing is voluntary and operates on the PEPPOL network. GST returns must be filed through myIR on a monthly, two-monthly, or six-monthly filing cycle depending on turnover.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Under section 11(1) of the Goods and Services Tax Act 1985, goods are zero-rated when the supplier exports them, or a GST-registered recipient exports them, within 28 days of supply, with the supplier retaining statutory evidence of export. Under section 11A of the same Act, services are zero-rated when supplied to a person who is not resident in New Zealand and is outside New Zealand at the time the services are performed, excluding services directly connected with New Zealand land or New Zealand goods and certain services performed in New Zealand. For AI avatar video-generation SaaS, the digital service supplied to a non-resident recipient qualifies for zero-rating if the supplier holds reliable records showing the recipient's non-resident status, offshore presence or location (e.g., IP geolocation, billing country, business registration address), and the foreign delivery of the service. If the same supply is made through a merchant-of-record payment processor, GST characterisation should be reviewed against the underlying commercial agreement. New Zealand GST law does not impose a fixed foreign-exchange repatriation deadline; the 180-day figure recorded in this dossier is a conservative internal audit benchmark and should not be treated as a statutory condition.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: New Zealand Customs Export Declaration (Export Entry) lodged through the Trade Single Window for exported goods
Bill of Lading, Air Waybill, or postal/courier export documentation evidencing physical removal from New Zealand
Commercial invoice, supply contract or purchase order, and proof of technical or digital service delivery

Foreign exchange remittance evidence from the non-resident customer (e.g., SWIFT MT103, bank credit advice, or Stripe/Paddle settlement records); New Zealand does not issue a separate Inward Remittance Certificate (FIRC), so bank and FX records are the FIRC-equivalent
For digital services: non-resident status declaration, IP geolocation logs, customer billing address, and payment processor records showing offshore consumption
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Inland Revenue may reassess unsubstantiated zero-rating and claw back GST at 15%, plus use-of-money interest and shortfall penalties under the Tax Administration Act 1994. Standard assessments may generally be amended within four years, with no time limit for fraudulent, wilfully misleading, or evasive returns. Shortfall penalties include 20% for lack of reasonable care or an unacceptable tax position, 100% for an abusive tax position, and 150% for evasion or similar. Knowingly false GST returns can also give rise to criminal prosecution and fines. To defend a zero-rating claim, the exporter must maintain the full documentary bundle and, for goods, evidence of export within the 28-day statutory period.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Reserve Bank of New Zealand - Te Putea Matua (RBNZ)
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: New Zealand operates an open, freely convertible currency regime. There are no blanket exchange controls, no licensing of ordinary FX transactions, and no requirement to obtain central bank approval for dividend remittances, service royalties, intercompany loan repayments, or equity injections under the current or capital account, provided the underlying transaction is lawful and counterparties satisfy Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009 verification requirements. The New Zealand dollar is a free-floating, fully deliverable currency. The RBNZ does not set exchange-rate targets, does not require export proceeds to be converted, and does not impose a surrender ratio. Profit repatriation is unrestricted, subject to withholding tax documentation and standard anti-money-laundering due diligence. The principal transactional controls are prudential and regulatory rather than FX: banks must sight commercial substance for high-value wires; transactions with sanctioned parties or unexplained ownership structures may be declined; and Overseas Investment Act 2005 consent can be required for certain foreign investments involving sensitive land, fishing quota, or significant business assets. This regulatory posture is well-suited to a global software-as-a-service treasury for AI avatar video generation, allowing multi-currency invoicing, rapid reinvestment, and clean dividend payments.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No statutory surrender timeline and no mandatory conversion ratio exist in New Zealand. Exporters may retain 100% of foreign-currency receipts indefinitely or convert them at their chosen bank as commercial market conditions dictate. For bank onboarding, the underlying sales invoice or contract must be retained, and if the proceeds exceed the bank's reporting thresholds, an AML/CFT onward reporting threshold report may be filed. There is no central-bank approval, no conversion certificate, and no requirement to remit export earnings to a designated government account.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Tier-2 collection-only viability. Offshore EMIs and payment facilitators, including Stripe and Paddle, are not RBNZ-registered banks and cannot legally hold demand deposits or operate as a full corporate banking relationship in New Zealand. They are not legally barred from servicing this entity for SaaS card collection and subscription invoicing, but they cannot replace a licensed bank for equity escrow, payroll, PAYE tax payments, treasury hedging, or physical custody of share capital. The recommended structure is to use Stripe and Paddle as the front-end collection engines and to sweep settlement balances daily into an NZD operating account at a licensed tier-1 NZ bank. Multi-currency EMIs such as Wise or Revolut Business may be used as supplementary conversion and sub-ledger rails, but the primary treasury, capital verification, and liquidity buffers must remain with a domestic registered bank. The legal boundary is defined by the Reserve Bank of New Zealand Act 1989, the Financial Markets Conduct Act 2013, and the AML/CFT Act 2009; any EMT without a New Zealand banking licence must clearly act as a payment intermediary, not as a deposit-taker.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: New Zealand company law requires NZ_LTD to maintain at least one director who is a New Zealand resident, or an eligible Australian-resident director in limited circumstances. There is no statutory mandate for every director to appear physically in a branch; however, tier-1 banks typically require the resident director to attend an initial face-to-face or supervised remote video KYC interview. Non-resident directors can usually complete identity verification through certified true copies of passports and proof-of-address documents prepared by an NZ-registered lawyer or accountant, with remote video attestation accepted under current AML/CFT practice. Consular proxy opening is permitted only at the discretion of each bank's product policy; many banks require a notarized and apostilled power of attorney plus a pre-approval from their compliance committee. The onboarding mandate should therefore assume that one substantive resident director or a New Zealand legal counsel holding a valid power of attorney will be available in person for the final account sign-off.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Apparent absence of genuine New Zealand substance, with all AI engineering and video-generation operations performed offshore while the NZ board is entirely remote.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide the Companies Office certificate of incorporation, registered office lease, substantive resident director appointment and declaration, local payroll records, office or co-working utilisation evidence, board packs demonstrating NZ-based treasury and governance decisions, an operational substance memorandum, and a business plan for AI avatar video generation.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Opacity in the beneficial ownership chain where the ultimate owner is a discretionary trust, an offshore private holding company, or a high-net-worth investor with wealth accumulated through cryptocurrency trading that cannot be easily traced.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Submit the complete trust deed or certified extracts, trustee resolutions, register of significant controllers, source-of-wealth statement for cryptocurrency exits including exchange statements and wallet flow diagrams, a tax assessment or accountant's letter confirming tax treatment, an existing tier-1 bank introduction letter, and independent legal opinion confirming that the ownership structure has no deceptive layering.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unexplained cross-border SaaS revenue concentration showing rapid subscription volume from Stripe and Paddle with mismatched customer jurisdictions, high refund volatility, or elevated chargeback risk.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide Stripe and Paddle merchant settlement statements, order-level export reports, B2B customer contracts, refund and chargeback history, software terms of service, privacy policy and Privacy Act 2020 compliance documentation, IP ownership and licence certificates, plus a board-approved treasury forecast explaining settlement lags, FX concentration, and refund buffers.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Adverse media, sanction-list hits, or PEP-family linkage on one or more directors or ultimate beneficial owners due to a prior unrelated e-gaming, crypto, or jurisdiction-hopping corporate history.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Deliver an independent sanctions and PEP screening report from a commercial vendor, public registry searches, self-declaration of PEP status, police clearance or certificate of good conduct from all countries of residence, professional biographies of every director and UBO, regulatory closure or disposal letters from previous corporate vehicles, and a remedial compliance programme with a clear source-of-wealth trail.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Route every equity injection through a licensed bank using SWIFT MT103 from the investor's own audited banking relationship. The payment narrative should state 'equity subscription for NZ_LTD' and the bank's FX purpose code should be classified as direct investment/equity capital under the bank's internal regulatory taxonomy. No RBNZ approval is required for ordinary share capital because the New Zealand dollar is fully convertible, but the bank will require the share allotment resolution, updated share register, investor identification documents, and an explanation of the commercial purpose of the AI video-generation treasury. If the investment involves sensitive New Zealand land, fishing quota, or significant business assets, Overseas Investment Office consent must be assessed before the injection. There is no statutory capital verification process in New Zealand; instead, the auditor will issue a share-capital confirmation memo for the financial statements and bank onboarding file.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Use SWIFT MT103 for royalty payments, licensing fees, contract engineering, SaaS infrastructure costs, and vendor settlements, with the underlying invoice attached in the regulatory record. Use an irrevocable documentary Commercial Letter of Credit at sight for physical merchandise or heavy equipment purchases such as GPU clusters and video-rendering servers. Use Documentary Collections, either documents against payment or documents against acceptance, only where a physical trade relationship with a buyer in Asia or the Pacific requires transport document settlement. For local payroll, PAYE, GST, and supplier payments, use the New Zealand BECS clearing system within the primary NZD operating account. Maintain a pooled USD/EUR/AUD multi-currency account with the tier-1 bank to reduce unnecessary spot conversions, and ensure every outbound payment is matched to an approved purpose code for AML/CFT recordkeeping and tax reporting.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Plain-vanilla deliverable FX forwards on NZD/USD, NZD/EUR, NZD/CNH, and NZD/AUD for up to 24 months, executed under an ISDA 2002 Master Agreement and a Credit Support Annex with daily margin, which is the primary permissible hedge for trade receivables and software subscription revenue.

Non-deliverable forwards are permitted only for receipts denominated in emerging-market currencies that lack a fungible deliverable market in New Zealand, such as certain Asia-Pacific or African currencies; an NDF is not needed or advisable for NZD itself because the New Zealand dollar is freely floating and fully deliverable.

Cross-currency swaps covering NZD versus USD, EUR, or AUD are permissible for long-term balance-sheet hedging of foreign-currency debt and capital investment, subject to RBNZ over-the-counter derivatives margin rules, bank credit limits, and ISDA collateralisation; no hedging instrument may be used solely for speculative spread activity without a documented underlying exposure.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Return of a Limited Company
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: New Zealand Companies Office (Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment - MBIE, Registrar of Companies)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 20 working days after the anniversary of the company's incorporation date each year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: No monetary penalty or statutory interest applies to late filing. However, if the annual return is not filed within 20 working days after the anniversary date, the Registrar may issue a notice of intention to remove the company from the New Zealand Register. The company is then removed 20 working days after service of the notice unless an objection is lodged. Administrative strike-off results in dissolution, loss of legal personality, and asset freezing. Restoration of a removed company is discretionary, subject to outstanding fees, compliance, and court/registrar restoration costs. Directors and shareholders who fail to comply may also face prosecution for an offence under Companies Act 1993.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Under the Financial Reporting Act 2013, an independent audit by a licensed CPA or CA (Chartered Accountants Australia and New Zealand) is mandatory for (a) any New Zealand 'issuer' company, and (b) any 'large' non-issuer company. A non-issuer company is 'large' for a financial year if it meets any two of the following three thresholds in both the current and the immediately preceding financial year: (i) total assets at balance date exceed NZD 60 million (approximately USD 37 million); (ii) total turnover or revenue exceeds NZD 30 million (approximately USD 18.6 million); (iii) 50 or more full-time-equivalent employees at balance date. In addition, even if below these thresholds, shareholders holding at least 5% of the voting shares, the board, or Inland Revenue may lawfully require an audit. Any reporting entity under the Financial Reporting Act 2013 or a company in an industry with statutory audit requirements (e.g., financial services, insurance) is also subject to mandatory audit.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: New Zealand Generally Accepted Accounting Practice (NZ GAAP) as issued by the External Reporting Board (XRB): Tier 1 – NZ IFRS (full); Tier 2 – NZ IFRS with Reduced Disclosure Regime (NZ IFRS RDR); Tier 3 – New Zealand Accounting Standard for Small and Medium-sized Entities (NZ AS for SMEs). An AI video SaaS company that is not 'large' may use NZ AS for SMEs; a 'large' non-issuer must apply Tier 1 or Tier 2 standards.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: New Zealand does not yet operate a separate recurring annual UBO return, but under the Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009 (AML/CFT), the company must identify, verify, and continuously maintain beneficial ownership records for any individual who owns or controls 25% or more of shares or voting rights, or who otherwise exercises ultimate control. Any share transfer, director change, or other control event must be notified to the Companies Office within 30 days of the change, using the appropriate update form. The annual return itself confirms the exact shareholder and director structure as of the anniversary date and must be accurate to ensure underlying beneficial ownership records are trustworthy. Registers and UBO information must be kept at the registered office and be available for inspection by enforcement authorities.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Directors and their details
Register of Share Allocations (if not combined with members)
Minute Book of resolutions and committee meetings

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 250 - 650 per year (typical NZ registered agent and registered office service fee)
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 7,500 - 20,000 per year (mandatory only if the statutory thresholds are met; exempt small companies will have a zero statutory audit fee unless a voluntary audit is commissioned)

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Statutory R&D tax credit equal to 15% of eligible R&D expenditure incurred in New Zealand; no patent box, no geographic free-zone tax holiday, and no exemption regime for active foreign income. The imputation credit system permits franking of shareholder distributions and can reduce the combined corporate-shareholder tax burden on resident shareholders; however, non-resident shareholders remain subject to non-resident withholding tax.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: IR4 – Company Income Tax Return; filed electronically through Inland Revenue's myIR portal or via a tax agent's e-file channel.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: For a standard 31 March balance date, the IR4 return must be filed on or before 31 March of the following income year unless a valid extension has been granted. Provisional tax installments are ordinarily due on 28 August, 15 January and 7 May, and terminal tax is payable at the same filing due date.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total assessable income from all sources.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Declare worldwide income before any deduction. An AI avatar SaaS company must include subscription and usage-based revenue from foreign customers, license fees, and all services performed remotely from New Zealand. Do not net foreign source losses unless permitted by statute.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: New Zealand-source digital services and software export revenue.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Separately disclose revenue earned from non-resident customers through Stripe/Paddle. While software exports are zero-rated for GST, they remain taxable for income tax if the NZ entity is the seller. Do not classify SaaS recurring fees as exempt royalties unless a genuine transfer of IP rights has occurred; apply the transfer pricing arm's length standard.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Cross-border related-party transactions and transfer pricing adjustments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Identify every transaction with non-resident related parties, including founders, affiliate distributors, IP-holding shell companies and service hubs. Enter the arm's length consideration actually used. If the aggregate value of cross-border related-party transactions equals or exceeds NZD 10 million, attach the Local File/Master File and a TP policy note. A 2% cost-plus return to the New Zealand developer while investors offshore capture 98% of residual profit will be challenged.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Operating deductions and specified apportionable deductions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Claim only deductions connected to assessable income. Exclude R&D credits claimed elsewhere and non-deductible distributions. Include director fees, cloud infrastructure, legal fees, AI compute costs, and royalties paid onward. Comply with the business continuity and record-keeping rules; do not claim fictitious vendor invoices created for the purpose of stripping profits.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net taxable income / loss before adjustment and loss carry-forward claim.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Align the loss carry-forward schedule with the registered company's shareholding continuity of 49% or more (or the business continuity test). A transfer-pricing downward adjustment cannot be booked in the tax return if it has not first been accepted by the IRD; any reduction in taxable income must be supported by an IPA, AP, or sufficient TP documentation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Non-resident withholding tax (NRWT) deducted from dividends, interest and royalties paid to non-residents.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: State the NRWT withheld from outbound dividends (30% statutory), interest (15% statutory) and royalties (15% statutory) on Box 6. Complete an NRWT rate declaration and retain the beneficiary's Certificate of Tax Residence. If no treaty reduction has been validated, withhold at the statutory rate.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax treaty relief declarations and certificate on file.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: List each non-resident recipient of dividends, interest, or royalties for whom a lower NRWT rate was applied because of an applicable DTA. Identify the jurisdiction, treaty article, amount paid, and the effective date of the Tax Residency Certificate. Keep the beneficial ownership statement proving the recipient has real economic substance and not merely a mailbox address in the treaty country.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Imputation credit account (ICA) balance and dividend disclosure.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report the debits and credits of the ICA. If the company has retained earnings and accumulated credits, ensure a sufficient balance before the dividend is declared. Directors should ensure any resolution is supported by cash flow projections showing the company can pay the resulting NRWT.

If a refund arises, confirm no outstanding tax debt subject to departure prohibition order. For non-resident investors, refunds are unlikely because all cross-border distributions are subject to withholding; arrange payment of terminal tax in advance to avoid use-of-money interest.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing of IR4 attracts an initial late filing penalty that escalates daily up to NZD 1,000. Late payment penalties accrue at up to 1% per month on unpaid tax, plus statutory use-of-money interest. Understatement penalties range from 20% (unacceptable tax position) to 100% (abusive tax position) and 150% for evasion or similar act. Tax evasion is prosecuted as an offence under the Tax Administration Act 1994; conviction may result in imprisonment for up to 5 years and fines up to NZD 250,000 for a body corporate / NZD 50,000 for individuals.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 30% NRWT on all dividends paid by an NZ-resident company to a non-resident shareholder, unless a DTA reduces the rate. Fully imputed dividends may, in certain circumstances, be subject to a lower rate or to the approved issuer levy alternative, but a payment to a treaty-shopping channel without a proper certificate is assessed at 30%.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke DTA relief: (1) identify the applicable treaty article and confirm that the recipient is a resident of the treaty state; (2) obtain an original Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) issued by the foreign jurisdiction's competent authority for the relevant tax year; (3) execute a beneficial ownership certificate and obtain updated AML/KYC identity evidence (passport, board authority, address) for the payee; (4) lodge the TRC and NRWT rate declaration with Inland Revenue before or at the time of filing the IR4/IR3; and (5) retain a written analysis showing the payee has economic substance and is not a conduit. Inland Revenue will reject reduced-rate NRWT if the documentation is incomplete or the recipient cannot prove beneficial ownership.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory royalty NRWT is 15% and statutory interest NRWT is 15%, but a shareholder-lender may be able to divert to the Approved Issuer Levy (AIL) of 2% on qualifying interest. DTA rates commonly reduce royalty withholding to 5% or 10% (depending on treaty) and interest to 5% or 10% (depending on treaty and creditor status). Reduced treaty rates never apply automatically; a TRC and beneficial ownership file is required for each payment stream.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: NZD 10,000,000 in cross-border related-party transactions (aggregate consideration) triggers mandatory contemporaneous transfer pricing documentation in the form of Master File and Local File under IRD's enforcement practice.
approved_arm_length_methodologies: CUP, Resale Price, Cost Plus, TNMM, Profit Split
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: New Zealand has no separate Economic Substance Regulations register, but a New Zealand-resident company seeking treaty benefits or using a parent company in a low-tax jurisdiction must demonstrate core income-generating activities (CIGA) in New Zealand--shareholder discipline, board control, product research, AI model development, and substantial staff presence. A paper-only shell will be disregarded and its transactions recharacterised under the general anti-avoidance rule and anti-conduit principles.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The NZ AI company sells its avatar video generation software to a related offshore distributor at a 2% cost-plus price and records zero profit in NZ, while the offshore distributor resells the same software to end-users with an 80% gross margin. The company intentionally fails to prepare TP documentation and classes SaaS subscription income as a royalty paid to the offshore shell.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The Commissioner will invoke the arm's length adjustment under the Income Tax Act 2007 (Subpart GC, ss GC 13-GC 15) and reassess taxable income at 28%. The resulting shortfall triggers a 150% evasion shortfall penalty under Tax Administration Act 1994 s 141C, use-of-money interest under s 120, and potential prosecution under s 143B of the Tax Administration Act 1994, punishable by imprisonment for up to 5 years and/or a fine up to NZD 50,000 (individual) or NZD 250,000 (corporate).
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly approve the underpriced cross-border sale or destroy TP evidence become personally liable for the company's unpaid tax; the Crown may pierce the corporate veil and obtain a civil restitution order. The director may be sued for the full tax shortfall, disqualified from holding office under the Companies Act 1993, prohibited from leaving New Zealand by a departure prohibition order until the tax debt is settled, and, on conviction, sentenced to imprisonment as a person concerned in the company's management.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: A non-resident investor routes subscription profits through a zero-tax jurisdiction to which no transparent DTA applies, causes the NZ Ltd to declare a large dividend to that offshore entity, and no NRWT is deducted on the ground of treaty relief, despite no valid Tax Residency Certificate or beneficial ownership documentation being held by the company.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The IRD will disallow treaty relief and assess NRWT at 30% on the full dividend, with the NZ payer held directly liable for the unrecovered withheld tax. The company will incur a shortfall penalty of 100% under s 141B (or 150% under s 141C if deliberate), interest, and potential criminal fines. The arrangement, if artificial, is void as a sham and the payments are recharacterised as assessable income of the shareholder in NZ.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign dividend declarations without ensuring NRWT compliance are jointly and severally liable for the withheld tax and any penalties; the veil will be pierced to enforce personal asset restitution. They may be served with departure prohibition orders, banned from acting as directors, ordered to pay compensation under the Companies Act 1993, and prosecuted for assisting in tax evasion, carrying a maximum prison term of 5 years.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Economic substance / AML and beneficial ownership fraud
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The NZ company is operated as a shell with no physical office, no local management, and no NZ bank account; payment rails Stripe and Paddle are used in a way that conceals the true beneficial owner of dividends and platform revenue, and the company files a zero-income return while claiming R&D tax credits for AI development that is actually performed offshore.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The R&D tax credit is denied (Tax Administration Act 1994 s 141A/141B penalties up to 100%), the zero-income return is reassessed, and the AML/CFT Act 2009 breach carries civil penalties up to NZD 2 million for continued non-compliance. The company may be removed from the New Zealand Companies Register, and ring-fenced profits are recharacterised as taxable in the hands of the true controller.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors/shareholders who mask ownership or permit the company to operate as an empty conduit face director disqualification under Companies Act 1993 ss 382-385, personal liability for reckless trading under s 383, anti-money-laundering criminal penalties including imprisonment up to 7 years, travel bans, restraint orders over foreign assets, and forced repatriation of funds under the reciprocal tax recovery measures.
